findings.codex_finding: Direct calls to authority_lib.derive_attachment_state() and authority_lib.evaluate_eligibility() - the two functions the v1.13 AUTHORITY_SURFACE declared AUTHORIZING - consume a forbidden-location sandbox evidence set and return ATTACHMENT_READY and eligible=true, bypassing the v1.13 wrapper-level governed-location law entirely. 93 of 96 checks passed; one BLOCKER and one MINOR.
findings.prior_defect: Reproduced against the frozen v1.13 bundle at 65895c6dedceadff012a08c1bafcdf9e92b65221 before anything was changed. A complete, mechanically perfect workflow authored under a sandbox root - the exact document evidence_authoring.derive_attachment_state() refuses with NOT_PRODUCTION_ROOT - was passed straight to the core: authority_lib.derive_attachment_state(tc, es, active) returned ATTACHMENT_READY and authority_lib.evaluate_eligibility(..., es, active) returned eligible=true with derived_attachment_state ATTACHMENT_READY. Root cause: v1.13 fixed V112-RP1 in the authoring wrapper, one layer above the authority. The core took a bare evidence-set dict and knew nothing about where it came from, so every v1.13 control was real and every one of them sat on a layer an attacker did not have to use. Same class as V112-RP1: a law enforced in exactly one place is a property of that place, not of the authority. The MINOR: EVIDENCE-SET-WORKFLOW.json still carried a stale test_root_override claim that the authoring API accepts a root parameter, which it has not since v1.13.
findings.correction: Location reconciliation is now part of the authorizing core. authority_lib.load_governed_evidence_set(session_id, active) is the ONLY door: it takes a session id and the active authority and nothing else, derives the canonical path from the frozen constant, classifies the root, session and document entries with lstat before anything is resolved, reads the document only from the path it computed, compares the document's own recorded location and session identity against where it was found, requires the recorded authority_root to be the frozen constant and written_under_production_root to be true, re-checks the bytes against the digest sealed at VERIFIED, and mints a location receipt under the registered domain vidtoolz.resolveLocationReceipt.v1. It returns a GovernedEvidenceSet whose __init__ refuses without a module-private token and which has __slots__ and no instance dict, so a dict, a namespace object, a subclass or a hand-computed receipt cannot fabricate provenance. derive_attachment_state_authorizing and evaluate_eligibility_authorizing (plus their by-session-id forms) accept ONLY that object and call governed_provenance_errors() FIRST, which re-derives every location fact from the live filesystem, so precedence is LOCATION AUTHORITY -> ATTACHMENT SEMANTICS -> ELIGIBILITY and a forbidden-location set never reaches readiness computation. The eligibility gate has no attachment-state parameter and recomputes the state itself, so no precomputed or diagnostic state can bootstrap it; it is fail-closed with reason code LOCATION_AUTHORITY_INVALID. derive_attachment_state and evaluate_eligibility are DEMOTED to a new AUTHORITY_SURFACE key, diagnostic_non_authorizing, with NON-AUTHORIZING stated in their own docstrings; their behaviour is unchanged. The authoring layer now delegates to the core's single implementation of the root resolver, the session-id law and the directory-entry trust check, keeping its earlier checks as DEFENCE IN DEPTH rather than as the only guard, and its own realpath alias check is gone because the core performs it. The stale test_root_override key is removed.
